sources.citation: Oropeza-Condori, Mayra; Miguel Frade-Flores; Marcel Barrero Mendizábal; Cecilia Tapia-Siles. 2025. Lenguaje formal de descripción para la Lengua de Señas Boliviana (LSB): una herramienta abierta para su uso en otras lenguas de señas. Investigación & Desarrollo (UPB, Cochabamba) 25(1): 97-105. DOI 10.23881/idupbo.025.1-8i
sources.note: Engineering paper (a domain-specific language and compiler for animating LSB signs as pose sequences). Not a linguistic description; the only prosody-adjacent remark is that a REPEAT function serves 'movimientos cíclicos o énfasis propios de la lengua de señas'. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Clark, Brenda. 2017. A Grammatical Sketch of Sivia Sign Language. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. xxii+340 pp. (= the 'Clark 2017' Glottolog cites for boli1236)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Phonology/prosody chapters concern Sivia Sign Language (Peru, lsv), not LSB. On LSB it says only (printed p.18): 'Publications mentioning Bolivian Sign Language focus on the deaf population (Holbrook 2009; Secretaria Técnica del CNCRD 2014) or technology (Martínez Severich & López Monje 2015)'; and (p.23) 'publications on the deaf population that uses Bolivian Sign Language often say nothing about their language'; only 16 Swadesh items available for Bolivian in her dictionary comparison. Nothing on LSB stress.

sources.citation: Holbrook, David J. 2009. Bolivia Deaf Community and Sign Language: Pre-Survey Report. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009-002. Dallas: SIL International. 13 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic pre-survey only; §4 p.8: 'There has been very little academic research related to LSB' — the only linguistic items are the Ministry of Education's Primer Libro de Señas en Bolivia (1992) and Morgan's (2000, 2004) lexicostatistic ASL comparisons; §6.1 p.10 gives one handshape example (CHURCH C- vs I-handshape). No prosody, no stress.

sources.citation: Wilbur, Ronnie B. 1999. Stress in ASL: empirical evidence and linguistic issues. Language and Speech 42(2-3): 229-250.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Not about LSB. Listed only because LSB is an ASL-derived variety (70-90% ASL lexicon per Holbrook 2009 and Wikipedia) and this is the standard account of what 'stress' means in a signed language (prominence via lengthening/tension), should the catalog decide how to treat sign languages; it cannot supply an LSB statement.
